To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for prediction purposes, the log-ratio approach is not recommended when the response is compositional, (ii) when the response is not compositional the log-ratio transformation should be used with care, and (iii) when the predictor is compositional the log-power transformation is the preferred method.

the use of a power transformation for regression analysis with compositional predictors is a viable alternative to the log-ratio approach when the data contain zero values, and that the use of power transformations for regression analysis with a compositional response is a viable alternative, even when the data do not contain zeros, and the power transformation can be data-based.

(1) when compositional data is used as a response variable, a power transformation of the data, based on the sample variance, is more appropriate than the log-ratio approach; (2) when compositional variables are used as predictors, the power transformation approach performs better than the log-ratios, but the difference is small.
